over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Gener8 Maritime, Inc. / Euronav NV realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired entity was absorbed via
> whole-company merger and deregistered, there is no periodic report filed by that entity
> alone; the realized record here is drawn from the acquirer's (Euronav NV's) own
> subsequent Form 20-F disclosures that separately name the acquired entities, plus the
> deregistration filing. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On July 10, 2018, the renamed entity (Euronav MI II Inc., formerly Gener8 Maritime,
  Inc.) filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of registration of its common stock
  under Section 12(g)/12h-3(b) and suspension of its duty to file reports; the filing
  recorded approximately one holder of record as of the certification date, and was
  signed by Milton Gonzales. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-044420, Form 15-12B]
- A search of the former Gener8 Maritime, Inc.'s (CIK 0001443799) EDGAR filing history for
  annual reports finds no Form 10-K or Form 20-F filed by that CIK after the pre-merger
  FY2017 10-K; no periodic report covering fiscal years within the ~2021-2023 outcome
  window was filed under that registrant. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001443799&type=10-K]

## Realized record of the acquired entities (Euronav NV's separate disclosure)
- Euronav NV's Form 20-F for fiscal year 2022 (filed April 12, 2023) states: "On June 12,
  2018 we completed the merger with Gener8 Maritime Inc. (Gener8) ... whereby Gener8
  became our wholly-owned subsidiary," and describes Gener8 at the merger date as owning
  a fleet of 29 tankers (21 VLCC, six Suezmax, two LR1 vessels; approximately 7.4 million
  dwt). [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- The same Form 20-F states, regarding the vessel-owning entities acquired in the merger:
  "All of the vessels have been transferred to Euronav NV in 2018. The Group liquidated a
  majority of those subsidiaries in 2019 and 2020." [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- As of December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020, Euronav's "Group entities" note lists Euronav
  MI II Inc. (formerly Gener8 Maritime, Inc.), Gener8 Maritime Subsidiary II Inc., Gener8
  Maritime Subsidiary New IV Inc., and Gener8 Maritime Management LLC — each a Marshall
  Islands entity — as 100.00%-owned Group entities in each of those three years. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- The Form 20-F discloses that the Group subleases office space to third parties in
  certain leased offices of "Euronav UK and Euronav MI II Inc. (formerly Gener8 Maritime
  Inc.)," with non-current sublease receivables of $1,591 thousand and $2,294 thousand as
  of December 31, 2022 and December 31, 2021 respectively. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- The Form 20-F discloses pending litigation as of the report date: RMK Maritime
  commenced proceedings in the London High Court against Euronav on September 30, 2022,
  seeking US$12,993,720 in damages for allegedly unpaid advisory services "concerning its
  merger with Gener8 in 2016 and 2017"; Euronav's defense was served December 29, 2022,
  and a case management conference hearing was scheduled for May 5, 2023; Euronav's
  management stated it believed it had strong arguments against the claim based on the
  written Advisory Agreement's terms. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]

## Items not separately disclosed
- Euronav's Form 20-F presents only Group-wide consolidated financial results; no
  segment-level revenue, net income, impairment, or vessel-operating figures specific to
  the former Gener8 fleet or subsidiaries are separately broken out in the filing, so no
  acquired-business-specific financial-performance scalar is sourced in this dossier.
  [UNVERIFIED]
- No source was found in which Euronav discloses a divestiture, write-down, or
  bankruptcy specifically attributed to the former Gener8 fleet within the ~2021-2023
  window; the entities associated with Gener8 instead appear, per the Group entities
  note above, as continuously 100%-owned across the window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Gener8 was absorbed through a 100% stock-for-stock merger and deregistered
  in mid-2018, there is no periodic report filed by the acquired entity alone; unlike a
  case with no public record at all, however, the acquirer (Euronav NV) separately names
  and discusses the acquired entities in its own Form 20-F: the acquired vessels were
  transferred into Euronav's ownership in 2018, a majority of the acquired vessel-owning
  subsidiaries were liquidated in 2019-2020, and four Gener8-associated corporate
  entities (including the renamed former parent and its former management subsidiary)
  remained 100%-owned Group entities through year-end 2022. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- Euronav's FY2022 Form 20-F also discloses a continuing third-party legal dispute
  specifically tied to the Gener8 merger (the RMK Maritime advisory-fee claim) and a
  continuing sublease arrangement involving former Gener8 office space. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]
- No segment-specific financial-performance scalar attributable solely to the former
  Gener8 fleet is separately disclosed in the reviewed filing; the realized record for
  this case is therefore documented on structural-continuity and dispute facts rather
  than on an income-statement or balance-sheet scalar. [SRC: SEC accession 0001604481-23-000004, Form 20-F (FY2022)]

[SLICE END]
